chunks: And whatever is narrated from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymun, I have narrated it from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, and from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah be pleased with them - from Abdullah ibn Jafar Al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khaṭṭab, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Hajjal Al-Asadi, from Abu Ishaq Thaʿlabah ibn Maymun. And I have also narrated it from them, from Al-Himyari, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿIsa, from Al-Hajjal, from Thaʿlabah.

key_terms.الْحِميريّ: Al-Himyari, a specific narrator in the chain
key_terms.ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونَ: Thaʿlabah ibn Maymun, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ: May Allah be pleased with them, a phrase of approval for the narrators
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I narrated it, indicating the author's direct transmission

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Thaʿlabah ibn Maymun verified in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq employs the technique of *tawatur* (concurrency) by citing multiple independent chains through his teachers—such as Abu, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil—to authenticate the narrations of Thaʿlabah ibn Maymun. This rigorous cross-referencing underscores the high reliability of the chain in Shia hadith scholarship, ensuring that the transmission is not reliant on a single, potentially vulnerable, source.
